metadata.title: Why it might be a bad idea to ‘flip’ SpaceX stock - MarketWatch

content.text:
17 hours ago
Why it might be a bad idea to ‘flip’ SpaceX stock
While some investors prefer to buy shares and hold them until they believe the time is right to sell, others are looking to just make a quick buck. But trying to flip SpaceX shares acquired through the initial public offering may backfire.
Many brokerages have installed policies meant to discourage retail investors from “IPO flipping,” or selling IPO shares soon after the stock is listed. In the U.S., most of the retail-oriented brokerages working with SpaceX have such policies. Charles Schwab is an outlier on that front.
SoFi, for example, won’t block its Active Invest members from selling their IPO shares. However, the firm will flag them as flippers and restrict some of their IPO-related activities. Robinhood notes that its customers who sell IPO shares within 30 days will be restricted from participating in future IPOs for a few months.
